metadata.title: TIMSS 2023 User Guide for the International Database
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center / IEA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This user guide documents how to analyze TIMSS 2023 International Database data using the IEA IDB Analyzer, including the availability of sampling and weighting variables in the database (see “Sampling and Weighting Variables” and Exhibits 2.10–2.11). The guide emphasizes that TIMSS involves complex procedures for drawing student samples and producing internationally comparable achievement and context estimates, so analysts should use the provided sampling/analysis weights when computing population-representative statistics and standard errors. The guide also explains that the IEA IDB Analyzer performs the statistical procedures needed for TIMSS analyses (e.g., merging files and setting up analysis modules), which typically incorporates the complex survey design information embedded in the database. Because this document is a user guide and not an empirical ML study, it does not specify a single weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight method for a particular model run; users are directed to the database documentation for the exact weight variable names and recommended analysis settings.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a user guide describing the TIMSS 2023 International Database structure, available files, and example analyses in the IEA IDB Analyzer rather than reporting a specific predictive model with a defined dependent variable based on cognitive plausible values. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable in the sense of this extraction task (no PV-based target is modeled as an outcome in the text provided). Missing-data handling is not reported because the guide focuses on what variables and scoring programs are available (including item response codes and missing-value codes) and how to run standard analyses, not on a single study’s missing-data strategy for an ML pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic subsample is defined in the provided text. The guide describes that the TIMSS 2023 International Database contains response records for over 359,000 fourth-grade students and nearly 300,000 eighth-grade students across participating countries, and it instructs users to select variables/participants and merge files in the IEA IDB Analyzer for their own analyses.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS 2023 User Guide for the International Database is a documentation and usage companion to the TIMSS 2023 Technical Report and Assessment Frameworks. It explains how the TIMSS 2023 International Database is organized (student achievement, process data, and multiple context domains), how to access public-use versus restricted-use variables, and how to merge data files using the IEA IDB Analyzer. The guide also provides example analysis workflows (e.g., average achievement, subgroup comparisons, linear regression with student context data, and analyses of international benchmarks) and points users to the database’s scoring programs and supplemental materials (codebooks, data almanacs, IRT item parameters). It does not present an empirical ML study with a defined predictive target, model comparison, or performance metrics in the provided excerpt. Instead, it instructs researchers on how to conduct TIMSS analyses correctly, including the use of the database’s sampling/weighting variables and the appropriate analysis modules for TIMSS estimates.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a user guide/data documentation rather than an empirical research paper. As such, it does not report a specific analytic sample with per-country Ns, does not define a single dependent variable for predictive modeling, and does not evaluate ML algorithms with performance metrics. The extraction therefore leaves ML- and PV-specific fields as not applicable/not reported and provides a methodological weight/usage summary instead.
